assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action) translated into long-acting agonists that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and very large, lasting medical impact are all strong; few discoveries of the last decades have changed clinical practice as broadly.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and isolation of active GLP-1 forms) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology, gut-derived hormone actions, therapeutic concept) are core on the basic side; Knudsen led the development of liraglutide/semaglutide on the translational side. Mojsov's contribution to the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is disputed and could reasonably displace one of these names; the three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized outcome trials, a decade or more of clinical use, independent confirmation across many groups. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue relative to its public impact.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov, Habener and others) is contested and I cannot resolve it from the supplied text.
A prize mixing basic physiology and industrial drug development must justify the translational laureate.
Long-term safety questions for the drug class are still being studied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and opened a new therapeutic modality, with approved products and expanding use in myeloma and autoimmunity. Conceptually clear and clinically decisive, and it builds directly on the T-cell biology honoured in recent prizes.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation, preclinical proof) and June (clinical translation, first durable remissions in CLL and ALL) are central; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept and Brentjens, Maus and others are not in the supplied credit, so the fairness of a three-person configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Substantial: multiple approved products, long-term remission data now over a decade for early patients, independent replication. Solid tumour efficacy remains limited and toxicity management is still evolving, but the core discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Original chimeric-receptor concept is not represented in the credited names beyond the listed three.
Allocation between Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and CAR engineering is unresolved.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and secondary malignancy concerns are monitored.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis synovium, and clinical proof that anti-TNF blockade produces sustained benefit, established cytokine-targeted therapy and changed outcomes across RA, spondyloarthritis, psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease. Clear, original, and of very large clinical impact; it also validated a mechanistic concept for immune-mediated disease.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly drove the concept and the pioneering clinical trials. My understanding, which I cannot verify here, is that Maini may no longer be alive, in which case only Feldmann could be a laureate; I therefore propose Feldmann alone. Contributions from TNF cloning and basic cytokine work (for example Kollias, Cerami, Beutler, Old) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: more than two decades of clinical use, biosimilars, extensive independent confirmation. Recognition is long-awaited rather than premature.
uncertainties: Status of Maini (possible death) is an unverified fact that affects eligibility.
Credit for basic TNF biology versus the clinical concept is not captured in the credited names.
Possible overlap with my own field makes me emphasize rigor in comparing it with other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy; successor inhibitors and resistance work (Sawyers) strengthened the paradigm.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme), Druker (preclinical validation and clinical trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation drugs) form a plausible trio. Upstream discovery of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, de Klein, Groffen, Heisterkamp) is not credited here, and Sawyers's role is more about resistance than the initial drug.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of survival data and independent confirmation. Recognition is timely to somewhat late, and the paradigm is well established.
uncertainties: Whether Sawyers or another figure (for example Buchdunger, Zimmermann) should be included is unresolved.
Upstream cytogenetic and molecular discoveries are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial opsins used to control genetically specified neurons with millisecond precision transformed causal neuroscience and has opened routes to clinical vision restoration. A clear, original and broadly adopted method with deep lasting impact on the study of circuits and behaviour.
assessment.attribution: The credited set of six exceeds three places. Nagel, Hegemann (and Bamberg) characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth, Boyden and colleagues expressed it in neurons and developed the toolkit; Miesenböck's earlier photosensitive-neuron work is a distinct claim. I choose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, acknowledging that Bamberg and Boyden have strong claims and the choice is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method: thousands of independent applications. Therapeutic translation is early but not essential for a basic-tool recognition.
uncertainties: Attribution among six or more credible contributors is the principal obstacle to a fair prize.
Primarily a research tool; clinical impact is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-modulating antisense drugs as a clinical platform. Clear causal path from RNA biology to dramatic benefit in infants.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and identification of the ISS-N1 target with collaborators) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis) are the core pair in the supplied credit. Singh, Hua, Rigo, Gillingwater and others contributed experimentally and are not credited, so allocation may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Moderate to high maturity: approval since 2016, durable follow-up data, and parallel gene therapy and small-molecule options confirm the SMN2 target. Long-term outcomes in treated patients are still accruing.
uncertainties: Credit among the several groups that worked on SMN2 splicing is not fully resolved.
Long-term efficacy in the oldest treated patients is still unfolding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP, and STING as its adaptor, defined a central innate immune pathway for detecting viral DNA, damaged self DNA and tumour DNA, with consequences for autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus, where I have a research interest), cancer immunotherapy and ageing.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS identification and cGAMP as second messenger) and Barber (STING identification) are the decisive contributors in my reading; Ishikawa shares the STING discovery, and Wu and Sun were key co-authors on Chen's work. The cyclic dinucleotide pathway work of Vance, Patel and others lies outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: strong mechanistic confirmation, but clinical translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved therapies, so recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic validation is incomplete.
Split of credit between Barber and Ishikawa for STING is uncertain.
I declare a topical interest through autoimmunity research, not a personal tie.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR and the mTOR nutrient and growth-factor signalling network established a central controller of cell growth and metabolism, with implications for cancer, diabetes, ageing and immunosuppression (rapamycin). Originality and breadth of impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Hall (discovery of TOR in yeast and its role in growth control) is the key figure; Sabatini and Schreiber contributed to mammalian mTOR biochemistry and the rapamycin-FKBP12 target. Heitman, Movva and Brown and others also contributed to early TOR identification and are not credited. The choice of a second laureate is not clear-cut.
assessment.maturity: Mature in mechanism and confirmed in many systems; clinical agents (rapalogs) are established though not transformative for most indications.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and uncredited early contributors is unresolved.
Some details of downstream signalling remain evolving.
